stem: Subtract and give the answer in simplest form: $\frac{{=b}}{x-{=p}}-\frac{{=a}}{x^2-{=s}}$ (the denominator may be left factorised).
solution: The L.C.M. of the denominators is $(x-{=p})(x+{=p})$.
Rewrite the first fraction over the L.C.M.: $\frac{{=b}(x+{=p})-{=a}}{(x-{=p})(x+{=p})}$.
The result is $\frac{{=b}x+{=b*p-a}}{(x-{=p})(x+{=p})}$, which cannot be simplified further. The domain is $x\neq {=p}$ and $x\neq -{=p}$.
notes: No book questions supplied; parent_question_id is a placeholder. Since a<bp, numerator constant is positive; numerator roots (-(bp-a)/b) never equal ±p (needs a=2bp or a=0), so no cancellation.
